turns.prompt_text: My hiboy scooter can run up to about 18mph, but usually only runs up to 13 mph
turns.response_html:
That 13 mph cap is incredibly specific—and it almost always points to one of two quick fixes rather than a broken motor or battery.

Here are the most likely reasons your Hiboy is capping out, ordered from easiest to hardest to fix.

1. You are stuck in "Comfort" or "Eco" Mode

Most Hiboy models (like the S2, S2 Pro, or NEX) have built-in speed modes.

  • Eco / Comfort Mode: Typically caps the scooter right around 11–13 mph to preserve battery.
  • Sport Mode: Unlocks the full 18–19 mph.

The Fix: Look at your display screen while the scooter is turned on. Look for a small number (1, 2, or 3) or a colored letter/icon indicating the mode. Double-click the power button quickly to cycle through the speed modes. You want it set to the highest mode (usually indicated by a red "S" or the number 3) to hit that 18 mph top end.

2. A Speed Limit is Set in the Hiboy App

If you've connected your scooter to the Hiboy smartphone app via Bluetooth, there is a slider in the settings menu specifically for "Speed Limit." It's incredibly easy to accidentally bump this slider or have a firmware update reset it to a default lower speed.

The Fix: Open the Hiboy app, connect to your scooter, and go into the settings gear icon. Look for the Speed Limit configuration and ensure it is slid all the way to the right (maximum capacity).

3. Low Tire Pressure (Pneumatic Models Only)

If you have a Hiboy model with air-filled tires (like the MAX Pro or certain variants), low tire pressure drastically increases rolling resistance. Running on under-inflated tires will easily rob you of 4–5 mph on flat ground and tank your battery life.

The Fix: Check your sidewall for the recommended PSI (usually around 45–50 PSI) and hook it up to a bike pump with a pressure gauge. If you have solid rubber tires (like the standard S2), you can skip this step.

Still stuck? If you cycle through the modes on the dash, the app speed limit is maxed out, and the battery is fully charged but you still can't break 13 mph, the scooter's firmware might be locked into a beginner mode.
